quote: Let X1 and X2 be two random variables such that X1 and X2 have the pdfs of the TIIPTL-G family given by f(x; alpha1, beta, xi) and f(x; alpha2, beta, xi), respectively. Then, we have X1 <=lr X2. ... which is negative if alpha2 < alpha1. Therefore, log[f(x; alpha1, beta, xi)/f(x; alpha2, beta, xi)] is decreasing, implying that f(x; alpha1, beta, xi)/f(x; alpha2, beta, xi) is decreasing. This proves the desired likelihood ratio.
family: TIIPTL-G family with pdfs f(x; alpha_i, beta, xi); baseline cdf G(x; xi); parameters alpha_i > 0, beta > 0, xi parameter vector of baseline
compared: two TIIPTL-G variables X1, X2 differing only in the alpha parameter

hypotheses.text: X1 and X2 have the pdfs f(x; alpha1, beta, xi) and f(x; alpha2, beta, xi)
hypotheses.formal: common beta and baseline xi; alpha1, alpha2 > 0

hypotheses.text: which is negative if alpha2 < alpha1
hypotheses.formal: d/dx log[f(x;alpha1)/f(x;alpha2)] = 2 beta (alpha2 - alpha1) g(x;xi)[1-G(x;xi)]^{beta-1} / ((1-G(x;xi))(2 - (1-G(x;xi))^beta)) < 0 iff alpha2 < alpha1, i.e. alpha1 > alpha2
hypotheses.source: proof (condition alpha1 > alpha2 is required for the stated order but omitted from the printed statement)

quantifiers: all x in the support; alpha_i, beta > 0
ambiguity: The printed statement asserts X1 <=lr X2 with no parameter inequality, but the proof shows the log pdf-ratio derivative is negative only when alpha2 < alpha1 (i.e. alpha1 > alpha2); the condition alpha1 > alpha2 must be understood as implicit. The paper defines X <=lr Y by f_X/f_Y decreasing, consistent with the printed proof. PDF renders 'X1lr X2' with the order symbol partially lost.
